tldr: Headlines across 12 countries converge on a single message: Iran will reciprocate immediately if the US returns to the June MoU. The military threat dimension appears only at the margins, and only Iran's own outlet repositions the SCO summit as an anti-unilateralism platform rather than a ceasefire appeal.

evidence.quote: 'immediately' reciprocate if US returns to June deal
Iran says it will return to ceasefire if US does
Iran urges U.S. to honour June interim deal
Tehran will 'immediately' reciprocate if US honours June MoU
SCO summit: Iran's opportunity to contain unilateralism

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to use 'olive branch' metaphor in the headline, framing Iran's conditional offer in conciliatory rather than transactional terms.
Uses 'claims' — 'Tehran claims ready to reciprocate' — adding a layer of editorial skepticism absent from all other outlets.
Only outlet to name the deal 'Islamabad memorandum' in the headline, aligning with Russian diplomatic terminology that no Western outlet adopts.
Uniquely foregrounds the SCO summit itself as Iran's strategic opportunity, framing the story as multilateral pushback against US unilateralism rather than a bilateral ceasefire offer.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents Iran as the proactive de-escalation actor waiting on US compliance, stripping away the body-text context of resumed missile exchanges and Hormuz tanker incidents — a framing gap that the divergence index will reflect across nearly all 12 outlets.
